# Glossary

| Term | Definition | Examples from this document |
|---|---|---|
| **Cross-reference (xref) or membership table** | A table that summarises assessments of membership of units of one (source) classification to units of another (target) classification. | See @sec-memb-table and @sec-formats. |
| **Source** | The classification being cross-referenced *from*. | In this document the source classification is TASVEG 5.0, the Tasmanian vegetation mapping. See @sec-source. |
| **Source unit** | One concept or mapping unit of the source classification. Each unit is assessed separately. | In TASVEG the classification units represent vegetation communities, see @sec-source.   |
| **Source unit id / Source id** | Unique ids for the units in the source classification. | `VEGCODE` column in the TASVEG Look-up table (@sec-lookup) | 
| **Target** | The classification being cross-referenced *to*. | In this document the target classification is the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology, see @sec-alignment.|
| **Target unit** | One unit of the target classification. | Here we use level 3 of the IUCN Global Ecosystem Typology: Ecosystem Functional Group (EFG), see @sec-source.   |
| **Target unit id / Target id** | Unique ids for the units in the target classification. | `EFG` or `efg_id` columns. Codes for EFG Codes are realm + biome + group, e.g. `T2.6` (terrestrial), `F2.2` (freshwater), `MT1.3` (marine–terrestrial shoreline), `TF1.6` (terrestrial–freshwater wetland), `MFT1.3` (marine–freshwater–terrestrial). |
| **Interpreter** | The person who made the assessment of memberships. | Here we refer to `interpreter` or `expert` interchangeably, see @sec-memb-table. | 
| **Membership** | An interpreter's estimate of the relationship between a source unit and a target unit. Target units have a broader scope, so they can group multiple source units. Memberships are interpreted as fuzzy memberships, such that a source unit might belong to multiple target units. This fuzzy membership is expressed as a continuous value between 0 (excluded from the group) and 1 (unambiguous membership). | See @sec-memb-table and @sec-formats. |
| **Assigned / not assigned** | Each interpreter assigns one or multiple target for each source unit with membership values above 0 (*assigned target*). The sum of membership values for assigned targets of a single interpreter should sum to 1. Potential targets (for example, those assigned by other interpreters) that are not listed by an interpreter, are considered *not assigned* and have a membership value of 0. | See @sec-memb-table. |
| **Not assessed** | The interpreter gave no record for the unit at all. This is different from "not assigned" and is never filled with 0. | See @sec-memb-table. |
| **Record** | One interpreter's membership for one unit and one target. Long format means one record per row. | See @sec-memb-table. |
| **Profile** | An interpreter's full set of memberships for one unit, across every target that any expert used for that unit. | |
| **Matrix table** | The data reshaped wide: one row per unit and interpreter, one column per target group. | `membership_matrix`, see @sec-formats. | 
| **Dissimilarity** | How different two interpreter' profiles are for a unit: ½ × the sum of absolute differences, i.e. the share of membership that would have to move to make them identical. 0 = identical, 1 = no shared membership. | `dissimilarity` | 
| **Similarity** | 1 − dissimilarity. 1 = identical profiles, 0 = no overlap. | `similarity` | 
| **Identical** | Two profiles with a dissimilarity of essentially 0 (below 0.001). | `share_identical` |
| **Expert pair** |  Two interpreter compared on the same unit. With four interpreter there are six pairs. | `expert_a`, `expert_b` |
| **Contested unit** | A unit where interpreter disagree. Units are ranked by their mean dissimilarity across all expert pairs. | `unit_disagreement` | 
| **Data checks** | Problems that are reported but not fixed: missing membership values, target codes that don't match the `XX0.0` pattern, and totals per unit and expert that aren't 1. | `check_*` |
